questions.question: Current assets are R840 000, of which inventories are R360 000, and current liabilities are R400 000. The current ratio and acid-test ratio are:
options: 2,1 to 1 and 1,2 to 1
2,1 to 1 and 0,9 to 1
1,2 to 1 and 2,1 to 1
2,0 to 1 and 1,0 to 1

questions.question: Khanya collects from debtors in about 30 days and pays creditors in about 50 days. This is favourable because:
options: It proves the company is insolvent
Suppliers are effectively financing the debtors' book — provided the 50 days stays within terms
Debtors are paying too slowly
It means stock never runs out

questions.question: Stock turnover of 8 times a year means:
options: Stock is counted eight times a year
Prices rose eight times
The average stock is sold and replaced roughly every 45 days
Eight percent of stock is obsolete

questions.question: Liquidity and solvency differ in that:
options: They are two names for the same test
Solvency concerns this month's bills; liquidity concerns survival
Liquidity uses total assets only
Liquidity asks whether short-term debts can be met; solvency asks whether total assets cover total liabilities in the long run

questions.question: Net profit after tax is R450 000 and average shareholders' equity is R3 000 000. ROSHE is:
options: 15 percent
17,5 percent
45 percent
8 percent

questions.question: ROTCE uses net profit BEFORE tax plus interest on loans because it measures:
options: Only the shareholders' slice of profit
The business engine's return on the whole pot of capital, before the funders divide the output
The dividend actually paid
The tax burden of the company

questions.question: With net profit after tax of R450 000 and one million shares, EPS is 45 cents. Total dividends of R360 000 give DPS of 36 cents. The pay-out rate is:
options: 45 percent
36 percent
80 percent — four-fifths of earnings distributed, one-fifth retained
125 percent

questions.question: Net asset value per share is calculated as:
options: Net profit after tax divided by shares in issue
The JSE share price divided by shares in issue
Total assets divided by shares in issue
Total shareholders' equity divided by shares in issue — what each share is worth according to the books

subtopics.title: Gearing, Returns and the Share Price

questions.question: ROTCE is 17,5 percent and the loans cost about 8 percent. This comparison shows:
options: Positive gearing — every borrowed rand earns more than it costs, working for the shareholders
Negative gearing — the company should repay all debt immediately
That the company is illiquid
That dividends are too high

questions.question: The risk that comes with higher gearing is that:
options: Shareholders must buy more shares
Fixed interest must be paid even in a bad year
The JSE delists the company
NAV automatically falls

questions.question: Khanya's shares trade at 380 cents while NAV is 304,5 cents. The premium exists because:
options: The market has made an arithmetic error
NAV includes future profits
The market prices what the balance sheet cannot show — expected future profits, brand and management quality
The share price must always exceed NAV by law

questions.question: EPS growth after a share buy-back must be interpreted with care because:
options: Buy-backs are illegal
EPS cannot change after a buy-back
Dividends are cancelled by buy-backs
Fewer shares flatter the ratio even when total profit is flat

questions.question: The directors' report should be read critically because:
options: It is the players writing the match report — the board's own account of its year
It is written by the auditors
It contains only numbers
It is addressed to SARS

questions.question: When analysing a published report, the audit opinion should be read first because:
options: It lists the dividend dates
A qualified opinion on stock valuation, for example, undermines the very ratios built on inventory
It contains the share price
It is the shortest section

questions.question: The King Code requires boards to act with:
options: Speed, secrecy, profit and growth
Authority, seniority, loyalty and silence
Responsibility, accountability, fairness and transparency
Caution, thrift, modesty and patience

questions.question: Insider trading and spreading false information about a company are:
options: Acceptable if profits result
Only unethical for directors
Legal on the JSE but discouraged
Both illegal forms of share-price manipulation, tested as ethics questions

questions.question: The shop has R840 000 of current assets against R400 000 of bills due soon. Aunt Nomsa's month-end verdict is:
options: More than two rand ready for every rand owed — the shop will not be embarrassed
The shop cannot pay its bills
The shop has too little stock
The shop must borrow immediately

questions.question: Even if the stock refuses to sell, the shop can cover its bills because:
options: The bank has promised an overdraft
Cash plus customers' debts alone give R1,20 for every rand owed — the acid-test
Suppliers never need to be paid
The owner will sell his bakkie

questions.question: Stretching suppliers too far is dangerous because:
options: It increases the current ratio
It reduces stock turnover
A damaged credit rating can bring cash-on-delivery terms, which strangles cash flow
SARS penalises late supplier payments

questions.question: Aunt Nomsa never asks whether the profit is big because:
options: Profit does not matter to investors
She cannot read an income statement
The shop makes no profit
A profit figure means nothing by itself — big compared to WHAT is the only question

questions.question: The shop's engine produces 17,5 cents per rand of long-term capital while the bank charges 8 cents per borrowed rand. Gearing therefore:
options: Works for the family — the bank funds, the family keeps the difference
Works against the family
Has no effect on the family's return
Means the loan must be repaid this year

questions.question: Borrowed money is called an amplifier because it:
options: Increases the interest rate
Makes good years better and bad years worse — the bank's charge is owed either way
Doubles the share count
Converts equity into debt

questions.question: The fixed-deposit test compares ROSHE of 15 percent with the bank's 8 percent to ask:
options: Whether the shop can afford new equipment
Whether the auditors are independent
Whether the extra seven cents per rand adequately pays the family for their risk
Whether tax was calculated correctly

questions.question: If the engine's return slid to 7 percent while the bank still wanted 8, then:
options: Gearing would work even better
Nothing would change for the owners
The bank would reduce its rate automatically
Every borrowed rand would cost more than it earns — gearing would eat the family's return

subtopics.title: The Price on the Board and the Value in the Books

questions.question: NAV of 304,5 cents answers the question:
options: What would each slice collect if the shop stopped today and everything sold at book value?
What will a cousin pay for a slice tomorrow?
What dividend was paid this year?
What is the shop's profit per slice?

questions.question: Cousins pay 380 cents for a slice with a book value of 304,5 cents because they are buying:
options: The shelves and fridges only
The shop's future — profits, loyal customers and management skill that no balance sheet records
A guaranteed dividend
Protection from tax

questions.question: Each slice earned 45 cents but was paid 36 cents. The nine-cent gap:
options: Was lost to bank charges
Went to the directors
Stayed in the shop as retained income, making every slice more valuable
Must be paid out next month by law

questions.question: Grandmother prefers the 80 percent pay-out while an expansion-minded cousin prefers 40 percent, which shows that:
options: One of them misunderstands dividends
The pay-out rate is fixed by the Companies Act
Dividends and earnings are the same thing
Neither pay-out policy is right in itself — shareholders want different things, and the directors must balance them
